text: The reported failures appear to be evaluation mismatches: valid alternative outputs were rejected, and two hidden cases contradict the stated constraints. I’ll preserve statement-correct behavior and add an independent correctness audit using valid generated cases and semantic checks for non-unique outputs.

args.old_string: 5. Before submission, audit performance at the maximum constraints.
args.new_string:
5. Before submission, independently audit correctness for nontrivial algorithms using run_python. Exercise the actual candidate implementation, not only a separately rewritten version of its core. On small valid inputs, compare against a simple brute-force/reference solver; use exhaustive cases when cheap, otherwise bounded randomized cases plus targeted boundaries (minimum sizes, equality/ties, empty or disconnected structures, and extreme legal values as applicable). Generate inputs that satisfy every stated constraint. Check feasibility and the objective, not just the shape of the output. For constructions or problems accepting any optimal answer, use an independent semantic validator rather than comparing output text. If run_tests reports a mismatch, inspect the failing case: distinguish an actual violation from a different valid answer or an input outside the stated domain. Fix genuine bugs and rerun checks; do not introduce sample-specific branches or sacrifice correctness to imitate one arbitrary answer. Keep this audit small and focused, leaving calls for repairs and submission.
6. Before submission, audit performance at the maximum constraints.

args.old_string: 6. When the examples pass and performance is justified, submit the program.
args.new_string: 7. When correctness (including any example discrepancies) and performance are justified, submit the checked program.
